messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A borrowed hand tool when two people disagree about who moved something. You may need the item yourself later. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "i put the tool back and mark the spot where the tool moved. “i think the other person moved first,” i say to the other. “i know the tool is yours.” i leave the tool in the corner. “i’ll prove it.” i leave the evidence behind. i wait for the other person to open the tool again."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "I rub my palm and take the tool. \"Move the edge,\" I say. I scrape once with my thumbnail, then turn it over. \"I mark the joint, then I say no.\" I mark the edge with my thumbnail, then leave it alone."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "I lean closer, then tap the worn grip with a knuckle. If one moves, I keep the borrowed tool beside the broken one. I tap again, then lean again, then touch the edge with a knuckle. If the other moves, I leave the tool beside the broken one beside the broken one."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "I put the tool beside the bench and leave the other person to pick it up. the dust marks on the bench keep their shape. I leave the paper beside it too, though the tool can keep its weight."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "i crouch beside the borrowed hand tool and test the handle with my thumb. \"i put it down,\" i say, then turn the handle until i see the old slot. \"i will leave it here for now,\" i say, and i crouch beside the tool."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "I put the tool down and rub my palm. “I move the old handle first. If it still catches, I leave it beside the drawer.” I put the new tool down and try the old one once."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "i put the tool beside the old nail. the nail stays cold. i move the seed husk from the step. the nail stays. i touch the nail once, then stop. the husk stays. the person who moved the nail looks at the nail. i put the tool beside the nail. the dust stays."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "i write the tool on the bench and leave it alone. then i check the other person’s hand. if they move, i leave the tool alone. i check the other person’s name, then write ‘I leave it alone.’"}, {"id": "R009", "response": "I pull the tool from the other person and put it on my lap. “That was mine,” I say. Then I look at the piece that was theirs."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "I photograph the tool and check whether the second person has moved it. My hand comes back, but my thumb slips and the second person drops it. I pull it back and photograph both. Then I check whether the third person has moved it. Sorry—i’ll photograph both. i’ll photograph the difference."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "i reach for the tool and feel the worn edge. i move it to the other person’s hand, then put the scrap in the drawer. i keep the original tool in case they keep it."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "you put the tool beside the person who moved. you look at the thing. “not here.” you keep the tool. the person leaves the thing on the step. you bring the tool close. nothing. you put your claw on the step. “not moved.” the person says the tool was there. you keep the thing."}]
